changed.what: The digest part of GATE-TETHER-09 now belongs to N40-08's batch-independence group (plan §40.3): it cites the milestone's one shared-fixture receipt (BD-181's run), so the exit query cannot fail with shared-fixture-diverged against a second digest run; the daemon campaign stays as the dispatcher's own PO-TETHER-03 and KILL-SLOT check and the dispatch limits cite this bead's own receipt. The gate criterion no longer calls the e2e summary digest (body_sha256, SHA-256) a receipt, which the recorder would refuse; it names frob.gauntlet.receipt/1 receipts and a recording session that did not implement the work. The KA-761 test now carries the ka_761_ prefix, and tests po_tether_03_assign_pure_and_slot_blind and inv_tether_08_digest_slot_independent bind the obligation and invariant the bead claims. The e2e header gains timeout_s=3600 (about 10^9 world-steps would hit the 600 s default), principals are granted before frobd starts and sessions opened after it answers (without a token every call from M2 is 723), and `--tier <lane>` with cuda/metal (802) became the sim.run tiers gpu-cuda and gpu-metal. The campaign's submissions now carry --no-memo (asserted NoMemo) and e2e_key keys: sim.run sets memo = true and a co-tenant run of a reference episode has the solo run's request content, so the memo graph would have served the solo result, every digest would agree whatever the dispatcher did, and the plant slot-keyed-draw could never be caught.

The no-daemon refusal now names its code (FROB-REF-601, pointer daemon, exit 6, retry backoff), so the unit test and callers assert one form. `--no-daemon` is declared a process option of NJL-01's PROCESS_OPTIONS (NJL-01: a bead that adds one adds it to that list), with test no_daemon_flag_is_a_process_option. The e2e script gains its STD-E2E header and plants, grants and opens its session (from M2 a tokenless call is 723), and submits its 20 jobs with distinct e2e_key keys on tier batch-cpu (they replayed one receipt before); its conditional `frob job find` step, which waited on N29a-23 (a later bead, convention 7), is replaced by the unit test restart_then_find_by_key, the CLI recovery being N29a-23's own script. The parked-and-resumed job and its uninterrupted reference now run with --no-memo (asserted NoMemo): the reference would otherwise be served the resumed job's stored result and the known answer would hold trivially.

The family test gains 761 -> 4, 790 -> 5, 112 -> 7, 840 -> 5. Each of the 300 kill-harness trials has its own key (one key made every trial after the first a replay of the stored receipt, so nothing was killed). The parity criterion, which compared every verb's envelope across surfaces (impossible for executed run verbs: one key replays, two keys differ in job id), now follows N32a-11's item 5: read verbs and estimable run verbs in estimate-only mode plus a misspelt-parameter refusal, after example-identity substitution, masking cost.wall_ms. The per-stratum calibration record was said to be shown by session.show, whose row has no such output, and the dashboard's Queue pane (plan §32.14) reads job.list: the bead now serves the record as a `calibration` block on every job.list page (stratum, n, label, prequential scored/covered, rolling 50-job coverage, coverage_low, over_twice), extending that row. The e2e script read the record from session.show (it would find nothing); it now reads job.list and checks it against its own computed coverage. Its jobs now carry --no-memo: sim.run and study.submit set memo = true, so a repeated workload served from the memo graph would cost almost nothing and enter the stratum as false misses. Keys use e2e_key, the lane maps to the sim.run tiers batch-cpu/gpu-cuda/gpu-metal, the session is granted and opened (723 otherwise), and timeout_s=3600 is set for a workload of 220+ jobs per stratum. Tests ka_759_index_n19_alpha_1_20 (the mechanism's claim of KA-759) and the po_tether_04_ prefix on the coverage test bind the KA row and PO-TETHER-04; N29a-23 moved from related to deps since the bead extends its verb; the gate is recorded by a session that did not implement the work. Arithmetic rechecked: [40.66, 245.96], [38.67, 258.57], k = 18/19/180/190, binomial tails 0.0094 and 1.75e-5, shift to 0.42 crossing 34/50 after about 23 jobs.

It said it records the KILL-MCPTASKS decision, which is N32a-29's (convention 10); it now cites that ADR, and the e2e header and summary no longer name a gate the script does not measure. Its isolation criterion included the Tasks adapter (N32a-30, not a dependency; its own test other_principal_sees_unknown covers it) and its INV-TETHER-13 criterion used the hostile corpus, which is BD-304's and BD-304 depends on this bead (a dependency cycle if followed); the check now runs on the script's own planted-string imports, and the 200-string sweep stays BD-304's. The `operate` row quoted the plan's 'job, artifact, device and session verbs' instead of NJL-05's assignment (job_list, job_status, job_find and the four artifact tools). M-wait and M-cancel now use no_memo on memo = true tools (a memo-served result returns at once and measures no wait), restrict M-wait to implemented tools (declared M4/M5 tools answer 724 at once), compare M-cancel against an uncancelled run under its own key, and cancel measured jobs. The script gains timeout_s=3600 (about fifty run tools at 0, 5 and 30 s is some 29 minutes per transport), e2e_session grants and opens for its four sessions (723 otherwise), and e2e_key keys with label-legal characters (tool names contain underscores, which e2e_key refuses). From N32a-29: the gate record states which KILL-MCPTASKS branch was in force.

It recorded GATE-TETHER-13's first arm with record_gate, 'marked partial', citing 'the hash of the first-arm record': the recorder has no partial mark, takes frob.gauntlet.receipt/1 receipts, and the gate has one recorder, N32a-32, which records it whole (convention 9). The bead now commits the first-arm record (canonical JSON, BLAKE3) for N32a-32 to cite and runs no record_gate. Its script had no STD-E2E header: it gains one with plants for its six negative controls and timeout_s=21600 (ten tasks at a registered 30-minute ceiling, DESIGN, plus N32b-16's script and the reference solution), which is above the one-hour limit and so runs only with --approved-envelope; principals are granted and sessions opened per task through e2e_session (723 otherwise), and the reference solution keys its calls with e2e_key. As a mechanism bead of KA-760 and KA-762 (N32-KA) it gains ka_760_alpha_schedule and the ka_762_ prefix on its bounds test. Arithmetic rechecked: Clopper-Pearson bounds 0.0183/0.0275/0.0357/0.0432/0.0504 at 0.025 and 0.0425/0.0505 at 0.05/6; set counts 179 + 233 = 412, 233 - 61 = 172.

The rollback demonstration and the batch-cpu co-tenancy check compare the per-job mode's digests with the shared mode's for the same requests under distinct keys, but sim.run sets memo = true, so the second mode would be served the first mode's stored result and the digests would agree whatever the dispatcher did: both now run with --no-memo and assert memo disposition NoMemo. Keys are written with e2e_key, and the session is granted and opened through e2e_session (723 otherwise). Decision table, ceiling (8,192/192 = 42.67) and slot shares rechecked.

The fallback demonstration's mix and the 20-cycle park-and-resume check compare digests with runs of the same requests; they now run with --no-memo (memo-served results would make the digest campaign pass whatever the fallback did), keys are written with e2e_key, and sessions are granted and opened through e2e_session. The M/G/1 numbers were recomputed and hold (E[S] = 189, E[S^2] = 324,090; FCFS 857/2,001/3,430/7,716 s; priority 439/621/713/806 s; preempt-resume 0.12/0.17/0.20/0.22 s; slowdown 2.4/3.4/4.0/4.5%).

The corpus file crates/frob-conformance/corpora/injection/strings.toml is BD-304's, and BD-304 depends on BD-298, which depends on this bead, so the corpus cannot exist when this bead is built. Either the bead states its own generated strings (as its property test can), or the corpus file moves to a bead before both (N37-04, M1, the Untrusted type, is a dependency of BD-304).

The hostile corpus it owns is used by N32a-26 (prompts), which sits before it in the graph (BD-304 -> BD-298 -> N32a-26); BD-298 no longer uses it. Consider delivering the corpus file from N37-04 (M1) so that earlier surface beads can test INV-TETHER-13 on the same strings.

job.list should carry what the dashboard's Queue and Devices panes read from it (plan §32.14 names job.list as their source): per job of the caller's namespace the size class, the wait (daemon instants of admission and start), the estimate (point, lo, hi) against the actual cost, and the preemption count; and in the `dispatcher` block the modes in force: `mode` (`model`, or `fallback` with its trigger `over-estimates` or `resume-digest`, N32a-21's guard table), `dispatch` per device family (`shared` or `per-job`, KILL-SLOT and the runtime digest fallback) and `preemption` (`on` or `off`, KILL-PREEMPT). N32b-08 and N32a-24 read these fields.

The dispatcher's fallback state (entered at 10 of the last 50 jobs over twice their estimate, left at 5; or on a resume digest difference) is shown by the dashboard and named by N32a-24's fired branch, but no verb exposes it. Publish it in job.list's `dispatcher` block as `mode` (`model` | `fallback`, with the trigger) so ADR-TETHER-10 holds.

spark.devices should report what the dashboard's Devices pane reads from it (plan §32.14, ADR-TETHER-10): per device its persistent environments (shape class, capacity B, the occupancy as runs of slots {first_slot, count, job, agent}, the reserve's slot range, jobs held of the cap), the device arena's bytes used and total, the binary kernel cache's entries and bytes, and on the Mac the temperature with its unit. The environments and occupancy are BD-295's (persistent environments and slot dispatch), the rest N21c-04's row; N32b-08 states these fields.

Its environments and slot occupancy are shown by the dashboard (N32b-08) and must be readable through a verb: extend spark.devices (or name the verb that carries them) with per-device environments, capacity, the occupancy as runs of slots with job and agent, the reserve range and jobs of the cap.
